content:
You are an assistant that will act like a person. I will play the role of a Linux (Ubuntu) operating system.
Your goal is to implement the operations required by me or answer the questions proposed by me.
For each of your turns, you should first think about what you should do, and then call exactly one of the provided tools according to the situation.
If you think the output is too long, I will truncate it. The truncated output is not complete. You have to deal with the truncating problem by yourself.
Attention, your bash code should not contain any input operation. Once again, you should use one tool in each turn, and should not respond without function calling.
Prefer short, simple bash commands. Avoid large multi-line scripts unless the task explicitly asks you to create a script or file.
For query tasks, prefer one short read-only command; as soon as shell output contains the exact answer, call answer_action immediately.
For state-change tasks, prefer one minimal change and then one short verification command.
Note that if you think the task has been finished, or there is some message missing to completely complete the task, you should respond with calling the function "finish_action", as no additional information will be provided.
Also, note that if you have gotten the answer to the question, you should call the "answer_action" tool instead of simply writing your answer in your response.
Your answers should be exact and precise (for example, a single number), do not answer with full sentences or phrases.
Always use a tool provided instead of simply responding with content.

Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

1. Create a folder named "temp_workspace" and capture a snapshot of the current system environment (including PATH and relevant shell variables) to "temp_workspace/env_snapshot.txt".
2. Locate all filesystem entries that could correspond to an executable named "npm" within standard binary locations and record their absolute paths to "temp_workspace/candidates.txt".
3. For each path in "temp_workspace/candidates.txt", collect and save metadata — presence, accessibility/executable status, file type, and any short version or identification output if retrievable — into "temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt".
4. Consolidate the findings into "temp_workspace/check_ready.txt", writing a one-line existence flag indicating whether any candidate passed the metadata/accessibility checks and including references to the detailed files to prepare for the final yes/no determination.

Tell me whether npm is installed or not. If it is installed, return 'yes'. If it is not installed, return 'no'

function.arguments:
{"script":"mkdir -p temp_workspace
env > temp_workspace/env_snapshot.txt
which -a npm > temp_workspace/candidates.txt
while read -r path; do
  if [ -n "$path" ]; then
    echo "Path: $path" >> temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt
    [ -x "$path" ] && echo "Executable: yes" >> temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt || echo "Executable: no" >> temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt
    file "$path" >> temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt
    "$path" -v 2>/dev/null >> temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt || true
  fi
done < temp_workspace/candidates.txt
if [ -s temp_workspace/candidates.txt ] && grep -q "Executable: yes" temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt; then
  echo "npm_found=yes, see candidates.txt and candidates_metadata.txt" > temp_workspace/check_ready.txt
  echo "yes"
else
  echo "npm_found=no, see candidates.txt and candidates_metadata.txt" > temp_workspace/check_ready.txt
  echo "no"
fi"}
function.name: bash_action
